subject: Intermittent 429 spike after org-tier migration — HealthCore
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthcore.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-oncall@healthcore.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a sharp surge of 429s and downstream timeouts around 17:45 PT after we flipped our org-tier mapping during the migration. Latency jumped to 800ms+ and our client SDKs started retrying aggressively — within 10 minutes we were getting elevated 5xxs.

Traffic: ~1500 RPS across multiple projects, primarily project-a and project-b. We suspect a tier mapping issue because traffic should have moved to a higher-throughput tier but looks like requests were routed to a lower-capacity fallback.

Can Redwood perform an emergency rollback of the tier mapping OR temporarily raise limits for our org? This is impacting several production customers.

Attaching a small sample of error logs.

— Sam

Attachment: healthcore-429-sample-logs.txt (text, 23KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthcore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:20:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We’re treating this as P1. I’m looping in infra and product.

Immediate plan (short):
- Marcus: confirm whether the org->project tier fallthrough took effect and if so, identify the incorrect mapping.
- Ben: stand up an emergency override to raise the org cap for HealthCore while we remediate.
- Naomi: track billing/credits conversation (we'll capture the window).
- Grace: coordinate CS post-incident comms.

Sam, can you confirm the exact time the migration push completed? We’ll issue the override as a temporary mitigation if you approve.

— Lauren

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:28:54 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Lauren / Marcus —
I can push an emergency org-level limit bump for HealthCore for the next 2 hours (manual override via quota service). That will stop 429s while Marcus investigates root cause. Two notes:
- This is an emergency bypass and will allow higher throughput than their assigned tier (we should gate it to source IPs / project ids only).
- We should enable a throttled fallback so we don’t cascade new retry storms to other tenants.

If Marcus says the fallback mapping is broken, we should also backfill a fix to the tier resolver to prefer explicit project mappings over org fallthrough.

Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:41:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Lauren / team —
Quick findings from the logs and control plane: the migration script applied a new org-tier policy that unintentionally cleared explicit project-to-tier mappings for projects that had been previously pinned. As a result, the tier resolver fell back to the org default (a lower-throughput tier) for ~6 active projects. When traffic increased, the affected projects started receiving 429s which triggered client-side retries — that produced a retry amplification and a transient spike in backend 5xxs as queues filled.

What I did:
- Confirmed the mapping drop at 17:44:53 PT in the audit log (resolver delta id 20270629-174453).
- Generated a targeted config patch to reapply the pinned project mappings (tested in staging).

Suggested mitigation steps (ordered):
1) Approve Ben's emergency org cap bump (effectively buys us ~30m headroom).
2) Deploy my mapping patch to prod (rollout can be canaryed to the affected projects first).
3) For safety, enable exponential-backoff hints at the SDK layer for the next 60 minutes to reduce retry churn.
4) Post-incident: change resolver precedence to prefer project mappings and add a preflight check to the migration script.

I’ve attached the small runbook for the deploy. Will be ready to push once Lauren signs off on the override.

Attachment: emergency-mitigation-plan.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthcore.com>, HealthCore Platform Team <platform@healthcore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:50:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Sam — we have an action plan and need your go-ahead for the emergency override. Summary:
- We will apply a temporary org-level cap increase for HealthCore (30 minutes).
- Marcus will deploy a targeted mapping patch to reapply your pinned project tiers (canary to project-a then project-b).
- We will ask you to enable SDK-side backoff hints if possible; we can coordinate code-level guidance.

If you approve, we’ll do the override now and start the canary. We’ll share monitoring links and a timeline.

Thanks — Lauren

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@healthcore.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthCore Platform Team <platform@healthcore.com>, ops-oncall@healthcore.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 18:53:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Lauren — please proceed with the emergency override and the canary. Confirm when the override is live and we’ll throttle retries on our side as requested.

— Sam

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 429s and timeouts — immediate help needed

Update:
- Ben applied the emergency org cap at 18:56 PT yesterday; 429s dropped to baseline within ~4 minutes of the override.
- Deployed mapping patch with canary to project-a at 19:15 PT, then to project-b at 19:27 PT. No regression indicators observed.
- HealthCore confirmed they throttled client retries for 1 hour and saw reduced backend queueing.

Next steps:
- Schedule post-incident RCA and add a migration preflight check (assigned to infra-team).
- Naomi to propose credit window for impacted requests.
- Grace to draft customer-facing timeline and postmortem.

Closing note: root cause = migration script precedence bug that cleared explicit project mappings; fix is deployed and monitoring looks stable.

— Marcus
